Rule written to the mapped path:

`/private/var/folders/11/m_kwnqr97632l_cjt0mhytvh0000gn/T/pstack-two-live-5OgTCn/agent/pstack-two/pstack-models.mdc`

## What I found

I enumerated the models actually resolvable by `Task` this session (`pi --list-models` + `ctx.modelRegistry.getAvailable()`):

- **deepseek** (`deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`)
- **openai** (gpt-4/4.1/4o, gpt-5.x, gpt-6.x, o1/o3/o4 families)
- **zai** (glm-4.7, glm-5.x)

There is **no Grok model and no Claude model** available. `auth.json` has `grok-build` and `claude-subscription` entries, but their provider packages aren't loaded, so neither family appears in the catalog. The skill defaults are only `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` — two families that are both entirely absent.

## What I did

Per your rule — *same family if available, else inherit-parent* — every role fell through to `inherit-parent`. Nothing here needed an effort bump: `inherit-parent` carries no effort token, and `large (xhigh)` only rewrites real slugs, so the budget label is recorded but every value is an alias.

- All 17 roles from the skill's mapping are present, in order, one line each.
- The 4 panel roles (`arena runners`, `arena cross-judge pool`, `architect runners`, `interrogate reviewers`) keep **two** `inherit-parent` entries each, preserving their two-way fan-out (the skill's rule that alias entries still count toward fan-out). Collapsing them to one would have halved the panel.
- `alwaysApply: true` is set, and the file was written only at the mapped path — nothing under `~/.cursor`.

I verified all 17 role lines are present and that every value is `inherit-parent`, which `resolveSubagentModel` always resolves to the parent model.

## Worth flagging

Because neither default family exists in this session, the rule is functionally "run everything on the parent." That is the literal result of your fallback instruction, not a partial mapping — so no role currently uses a distinct available model. If you'd rather split the roles across the models you *do* have (for example a fast `deepseek`/`zai` model for the tooling/worker roles and a strong `openai` model for the judgment/prose roles), say the word and I'll rewrite it — that would be a capability match, not a same-family substitution.

The rule applies to new sessions; re-running `/setup-pstack` updates it in place.

Unrelated to this task: the project has no verification skill or harness for driving a real app, so if you later want one, `/create-verification-skill` can generate it.
